tools.description: Push a branch of a checkout on this Mac to its GitHub repository, as the agent's GitHub App. The checkout is the folder the session works in (a container sees it at the same path). Pushes refs/heads/<branch> only: never main, master, the repository's default branch or a tag. Replaces the remote branch only with force_with_lease, against what the checkout last saw of it.

branch.description: The local branch to push; it is pushed under the same name.

force_with_lease.description: Replace the remote branch if it is still at refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch> in the checkout (git push --force-with-lease). Default false.

path.description: The checkout's absolute path (the session's folder or a folder in it).

tools.name: git_push

tools.description: Open a pull request from a branch already pushed (git_push) into base.

base.description: The branch to merge into, e.g. main.

draft.description: Open it as a draft. Default false.

head.description: The branch with the changes (branch, or owner:branch in the same account).

tools.name: pr_create

tools.description: Change a pull request's title or description (nothing else: not its state, base or reviewers).

body.description: A new description (Markdown); it replaces the old one.

tools.name: pr_edit

tools.description: Comment on a pull request's conversation.
tools.name: pr_comment

tools.description: A pull request: its state, mergeability, head and base, description and reviews.
tools.name: pr_view

tools.description: A repository's pull requests (50 at most, newest first).

head.description: Only those from this branch (branch, or owner:branch).

tools.name: pr_list

tools.description: A commit's check runs and commit statuses, and how many passed, failed or are pending.

ref.description: A commit SHA, branch or tag.

tools.name: checks

tools.description: A repository's GitHub Actions workflow runs, newest first.

event.description: Only runs of this event (push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, …).

tools.name: runs

tools.description: A workflow run: its jobs and their conclusions (failed steps named), and its artifacts.

run_id.description: The workflow run's id (runs lists them).

tools.name: run_view

tools.description: A workflow run's logs, as text: the last max_lines lines of each job's log (for a failed job, the lines up to its last error), timestamps removed.

failed_only.description: Only the jobs that failed. Default false.

job.description: One job: its id or its name (else every job).

max_lines.description: Lines a job at most (1-5000, default 200).

run_id.description: The workflow run's id (runs lists them).

tools.name: run_log

tools.description: Download a workflow run's artifact and unzip it into path: a folder that does not exist yet (or is empty) inside a checkout of an allowed repository, or under /tmp.

path.description: The absolute path of the folder to unzip it into.

run_id.description: The workflow run's id (runs lists them).

tools.name: artifact_download

tools.description: Draft a release (a draft only: never published; publishing is a person's).

tag.description: The tag it will have once published (e.g. v1.2.0); not made until then.

target.description: The branch or commit SHA the tag will point at.

tools.name: release_draft

body.description: New notes (Markdown); they replace the old.

target.description: A new branch or commit SHA for the tag.

tools.name: release_edit_draft

tools.description: A repository's releases, drafts included (30 at most, newest first).
tools.name: release_list

tools.description: Read a file from a repository on GitHub (or list a folder).

path.description: The file's path in the repository, e.g. README.md.

ref.description: A branch, tag or commit SHA (else the default branch).

tools.name: repo_file

tools.description: Fetch an allowed GitHub repository's branches into a checkout on this Mac, as the agent's GitHub App: they land in refs/remotes/<remote>/…, for rebasing onto main and for git_push's force_with_lease. Nothing is checked out or merged.

path.description: The checkout's absolute path (the session's folder or a folder in it).

refs.description: The branches to fetch, separated by spaces or commas (default all).

remote.description: The remote whose repository to fetch (default origin).

tools.name: git_fetch

tools.description: A pull request's inline review comments: path, line, author, body, and which they reply to.
tools.name: pr_review_comments

tools.description: The files a pull request changes, with their patches (each clipped to 4000 characters).
tools.name: pr_files

tools.description: A branch's commits, newest first.

ref.description: A branch, tag or SHA to start from (default the default branch).

tools.name: commits

tools.description: A commit: its message, parents and files with their patches.

ref.description: The commit's SHA (or a branch or tag).

tools.name: commit_view

tools.description: How head differs from base: ahead and behind, the commits and the files.

base.description: The branch, tag or SHA to compare against, e.g. main.

head.description: The branch, tag or SHA to compare.

tools.name: branches

tools.description: A repository's issues (pull requests left out; 50 at most).

labels.description: Only those with all these labels, comma-separated.

tools.name: issues_list

tools.description: An issue (or a pull request's conversation): its body, labels and comments.
tools.name: issue_view

tools.description: Reply to an inline review comment (pr_review_comments gives its id).
tools.name: pr_review_comment_reply

tools.description: Review a pull request with a comment. COMMENT only: approving and requesting changes are Logan's.
tools.name: pr_review

tools.description: Open an issue.
tools.name: issue_create

tools.description: Comment on an issue.
tools.name: issue_comment

body.description: A new description; it replaces the old.

labels.description: Its labels, comma-separated: they replace the old ones ("" for none).

tools.name: issue_edit

tools.description: Mark a pull request ready for review, or (ready false) turn it back into a draft.

ready.description: true (the default): ready for review; false: back to draft.

tools.name: pr_ready_for_review

tools.description: Bring a pull request's branch up to date with its base (GitHub merges the base into it), if its head is still the one GitHub last showed. Only pull requests from a branch of the same repository.
tools.name: pr_update_branch

tools.description: Merge a pull request once CI is green. Refused, with the reason, unless it is open, not a draft, into the default branch from a branch of the same repository, GitHub's mergeable_state is clean (behind: call pr_update_branch first), every check run on its head passed (statuses too where readable), and it touches no path CODEOWNERS owns unless an owner approved its head. Merges exactly the head checked; never bypasses GitHub's rules. Answers the merge commit.

message.description: The squash (or merge) commit's message (else GitHub's).

method.description: squash (the default), merge or rebase, if the repository allows it.

title.description: The squash (or merge) commit's title (else GitHub's).

tools.name: pr_merge

tools.description: Run a completed workflow run's failed jobs again (or every job, failed_only false). Only pull_request, push and workflow_dispatch runs from a branch of the same repository whose commit is still the head (of its open pull request, or of its branch): never an old commit's, a release's or a schedule's run. Its checks run again, and pr_merge waits for them to pass.

failed_only.description: Only the failed (and cancelled) jobs. Default true.

run_id.description: The workflow run's id (runs lists them).

tools.name: run_rerun

tools.description: Run a workflow that declares workflow_dispatch, on a branch of the same repository (main too), with optional inputs (a JSON object of one-line strings). Answers the run it made, with its id and the commit it runs on. Its checks are the workflow's own; nothing about merging changes.

inputs.description: Its inputs, a JSON object of strings: {"kind": "quick"}.

ref.description: The branch to run it on.

workflow.description: The workflow's file name in .github/workflows (ci.yml), or its id.

tools.name: run_dispatch

tools.description: Cancel a workflow run that is queued or in progress (not a release's). GitHub cancels asynchronously; never a force-cancel.

run_id.description: The workflow run's id (runs lists them).

tools.name: run_cancel
